task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Can role transferability be tested with n=24 units?
How should cut-heavy versus drive-heavy shaper categories be defined from play-by-play and graph-derived play-type records?
What reliability and sample-size constraints apply to comparing role travel between two player groups?
How should travel or portability of roles be measured across seasons, teams, or playoff contexts?
evidence_establishes: No earlier project study on this question, its shaper classification, or its portability measure was returned by retrieve_history (n_results = 0). Nothing about the question is established by retrieved evidence.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy shapers' roles.
Whether any shaper-style classification from the play-type records is reliable or stable.
Whether any role-portability measure is valid or has been validated in this data.
Whether n=24 units is adequate for any comparison; the retrieval provides no power or reliability benchmark.
own_inferences: 'Role travel' is not operationalised in the task statement. Without a definition (for example, out-of-sample performance of a role metric, or stability of role assignment across teams, seasons or playoffs), no hypothesis can be tested.
Classifying players as cut-heavy or drive-heavy requires thresholds on play-type shares. These shares are noisy at the player-season level, and a split of 24 units would leave very few units per arm.
Any apparent difference between groups could reflect minutes, team context, usage, or shot-distance mix rather than the shaper style itself.
The data span four seasons with partial 2025-26 data before the stated dates, so season-by-season comparisons may mix complete and incomplete samples.
uncertainties: The unit of analysis behind n=24 is not stated (players, team-seasons, or another unit).
The number of units in each shaper group is not given.
The exact formulas for cut-heavy and drive-heavy shares, and for role travel, are not specified.
Whether graph-derived play-type records match the play-by-play files has not been checked.
Whether an earlier project study exists outside the retrieval index is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: retrieve_history returned no records, so no historical evidence was available. The decision rests on the task statement and the stated data constraints (n=24, undefined constructs, partial 2025-26 data), not on earlier results.

blocking_constraints.text: With n=24 units split into two style groups, power to detect a difference in role travel is likely low unless the effect is very large.
Shares of cut versus drive possessions and role-portability measures are likely noisy at the unit level, and their reliability has not been established.
If role travel is scored using the same play-type or points outcomes used to define shaper style, the classification and outcome are not independent.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so it is unknown whether this question has been answered. No prior work is relied on.

risks.text: n=24 units gives low power for a two-group comparison of role travel, so a null result would be uninformative.
Player-level cut and drive shares from one or a few seasons may be unstable, and misclassification would bias the comparison toward the null.
Defining style and role travel from overlapping play-type and points data may build the result into the measure.
Usage, minutes, role on team, position and shot-distance mix may explain group differences in portability.
Selecting extreme cut-heavy or drive-heavy players on one season and then measuring them in a later season would produce regression to the mean.
Some play types or shot distances may have too few possessions per unit for stable shares, especially in partial 2025-26 data and playoff samples.
Rule, pace and style changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may make role portability differ by season and confound pooled comparisons.
Trying several style thresholds, portability metrics and season or playoff splits would inflate the chance of a spurious positive result.
Play-type and shooter attribution errors in the play-by-play or graph-derived records could misassign possessions to initiators and styles.

design.estimand: Not defined as posed. Minimum viable estimand: the difference in a pre-specified, out-of-sample role-portability metric between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers, adjusted for usage, minutes and position.
design.unit: Not stated in the task. Minimum viable unit: player-season with a minimum possession threshold, or team-season if that is what the n=24 denotes. This must be confirmed before analysis.
design.sample: The task gives n=24 units without group sizes. Before any analysis, the sample must be confirmed from the data files, with the 2025-26 regular season restricted to complete data (from 2026-04-13) and the 2025-26 playoffs restricted to complete data (from 2026-06-21).
design.power: Not computed. Before proceeding, a simulation must show that the design has at least 80% power for a pre-specified effect size. With n=24 this is unlikely unless the effect is very large, so the expected result is a precision statement rather than a test.
design.controls: Adjust for minutes, usage rate, position, team pace, shot-distance mix and season fixed effects. Use split-half or cross-season reliability checks on cut and drive shares before classification.
design.falsification: Use a placebo style, such as a shooting-share split with no theoretical link to cut or drive play, and check that it does not show the same portability advantage. Also check that the result does not hold when the style labels are randomly permuted within team-season.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary style threshold, one portability metric and one season split. Treat all other comparisons as exploratory and correct for them.
design.decision_rule: Proceed only if the pre-registered power simulation reaches the target power and reliability checks pass. Otherwise report the question as untestable with this data and do not interpret any point estimate.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, plus 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13 and 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21. Partial 2025-26 files are excluded.
